source: ASME B16.5-2025, Tables 2-1.1 through 2-3.19 (SI units), transcribed from a purchased copy supplied by the project owner. All 45 material groups, 16 temperatures, 7 classes. The document itself is NOT in this repository - see standards-source/README.md.
note:
The second hop of the rating lookup. The first is materials.ref.json's b165MaterialGroup: grade -> group. This pack is (standard, edition, group, class, temperature) -> pressure.

VERIFIED against ASME B16.5-2025 on 2026-09-24. Group 1.1 previously held an informed reconstruction; it was replaced, and the reconstruction's error is recorded under corroboration.priorReconstruction so the size of that kind of guess is on the record.

B16.47 remains UNVERIFIED and carries no curves. Series A and B share their ratings, so there is still no series axis here.

conventions.pressureIsGauge: Ratings are maximum allowable working GAUGE pressure.
conventions.interpolation: B16.5 permits linear interpolation between tabulated temperatures and forbids extrapolation beyond the ends. The points here are SPARSER than the standard's own tabulation, so interpolating them is coarser than interpolating B16.5.
conventions.noSeriesAxis: B16.47 Series A and Series B share identical pressure-temperature ratings; the series changes dimensions only. So there is deliberately no series axis here. It belongs on flange-bolting and on the flange row. ADR-008 section 11.15.

standards.note: Max class is 900: B16.5 reaches 2500, B16.47 does not. Class 75 is Series B only - VERIFIED from B16.47-2025, which tabulates dimensions for Class 75 under Series B alone (Table 37) while Series A starts at Class 150 (Table 32). seriesShareRatings is VERIFIED the same way: the 27 rating tables (3-28) are indexed by material group with no series axis at all, while the dimension tables (32+) are per series.

derivedClasses.note: Class 800 is not tabulated by ASME. API 602 clause 4.1.3: the ratings "are a linear interpolation of Standard Class 600 and Standard Class 900 pressure/temperature ratings listed in ASME B16.34". Class 800 sits two thirds of the way from 600 to 900, hence the weights. ADR-008 11.13.

appliesToStandard.evidence: Clause 4.1.3 interpolates "Standard Class 600 and Standard Class 900 pressure/temperature ratings listed in ASME B16.34". A Class 800 valve was being derived from the FLANGE tables - the same error, in miniature, that valve-pt-ratings exists to correct.

corroboration.against: API 602-2015 Table 2a, ASME B16.34 material group 1.1, SI units
corroboration.note: Applying the clause to B16.34-2025 reproduces API 602-2015 Table 2a to within 0.023 MPa on 14 of 16 rows. The two that differ are consistent with B16.34 having changed between the edition API 602 was drafted against and 2025 - not with an error on either side.

derivedClasses.undatedReference: API 602 clause 2 cites ASME B16.34 WITHOUT a date, and states that for undated references the latest edition applies. So for a project today the governing Class 800 rating is this interpolation of B16.34-2025, NOT the figure printed in API 602-2015 Table 2a. The printed table is a snapshot of the rule, and the rule is what the standard actually requires.

corroboration.whatThisIsNot: Historical. These figures are now transcribed from the purchased standard, so this block records what the PREVIOUS unverified reconstruction got right and wrong, as evidence about how much a confident reconstruction is worth.

internalChecks.check: Above Class 150 the rating is linear in the class number at every temperature, which is how B16.5 was constructed.
internalChecks.result: still holds on the real data, across all 45 groups

internalChecks.check: The API 602 Class 800 formula on the real Group 1.1 curve vs a manufacturer's published catalogue figure.
internalChecks.result: 1973 psi at 38 C; OMB prints 1975 psi

priorReconstruction.summary: The Group 1.1 curve written from working knowledge before the standard arrived was compared against it point by point. 36 comparable values: mean absolute error 0.42 per cent, worst 2.61 per cent. Every value up to 400 C was within 0.3 per cent; the whole 500 C row ran about 2 per cent high. It also carried only 6 of the 16 tabulated temperatures and had omitted Class 400 entirely.
priorReconstruction.theUsefulLesson: The one external spot check that had looked like a 3.3 per cent error of ours was the SOURCE being wrong: midstreamcalculator printed 1095 psig for Class 600 at 600 F, the standard says 1135, and our curve interpolated 1131. Internal consistency checks beat spot checks against unverified third parties.

crossStandardDiscrepancies.whatThisIs:
ASME B16.5-2025 and ASME B16.47-2025 rate the SAME material groups, and they agree on 2,089 of the 2,100 values they share - 99.48 per cent, to the last printed digit. These are the 11 cells where two purchased standards of the same vintage disagree.

NEITHER TRANSCRIPTION HAS BEEN ALTERED. Each pack holds what its document says. Silently correcting a standard to match another standard would destroy the only evidence that the disagreement exists.
crossStandardDiscrepancies.howTheyWereArbitrated: Above Class 150 a rating is linear in the class number, so the other classes in the SAME ROW of the SAME table predict the disputed cell without reference to either standard's opinion. Class 150 and Class 75 sit below that line by design and cannot be arbitrated this way.
crossStandardDiscrepancies.finding:
Of the 9 cells where the line can decide, it favours B16.5 in 8 - and in 7 of those the B16.5 value is within 0.09 bar of the prediction while B16.47 is 0.94 to 3.06 bar away. The remaining 2 differ by one digit in the last place in both directions and are rounding noise, not error.

The Class 150 case decides itself by inspection: B16.47 Table 20 prints 5.5 bar at BOTH 400 C and 425 C, while B16.5 prints 7.4 / 6.5 / 5.5 / 4.6 down the same column. B16.47 appears to have repeated the 425 C cell.

Reading: B16.47-2025 carries a handful of typographical errors in its SI rating tables. This is an OBSERVATION, not an authority. Where a project is governed by B16.47 the B16.47 figure is the contractual one, which is exactly why both are kept.
crossStandardDiscrepancies.policy: Record it, then raise a discrepancy - never refuse the write and never reconcile silently. A consumer asking for a B16.47 rating gets the B16.47 number; discrepancyFor() tells it that a sister standard disagrees.

cells.consistentWithItsNeighbours: neither - Class 150 sits below the line by design and cannot be arbitrated this way
